provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
Mechanism (in visible coordinates). The frame colour is read from the grid corner. The two non-frame 4-connected regions are the two panels. The design panel is the region holding more than one colour, and the canvas is the uniform one. If both were uniform, the program falls back to the d4-derived side.

The panel colour is read from the design panel's corner, which is always margin. Each single-colour 4-connected component inside the design panel is one shape. Its extent is compared with the design panel's inner range (panel minus a 1-cell margin) along the cross axis:
- A shape spanning the full inner range is stretched over the canvas inner range.
- A shape touching the low inner edge is anchored at the canvas inner low edge.
- A shape touching the high inner edge is anchored at the canvas inner high edge.
- Otherwise (outside the generator's domain) the shape keeps its offset from the low edge.

The coordinate along the separator is unchanged.

The factory specialises only geometry from d4, as follows:
- d4 in {0,2,4,6}: the panels sit side by side, shapes keep their rows and are placed along columns.
- d4 in {1,3,5,7}: the panels are stacked, shapes keep their columns and are placed along rows.
- d4 also fixes which side the design panel lies on (left/top/right/bottom), but this is only a tie-break fallback.

Reflections need no special handling. Low-edge-to-low-edge and high-edge-to-high-edge anchoring maps both panels consistently. All colour roles (frame, design panel, canvas, shape colours) are inferred from pixels, so palette permutations need no constants.
draft_notes.limitations:
I have not run any tests on this factory or the emitted program; the host checks are still pending.

The program assumes the constructor's domain:
- A single-cell frame and one frame-coloured separator line, giving exactly two non-frame panels.
- Rectangular shapes that are separated from each other by at least one cell.
- Shape colours that differ from the frame, panel and canvas colours.
- Every shape either spans the full inner range or touches exactly one inner edge. With left>=5 the generator's 2x2 blocks never touch both edges.

The 'touches neither edge' fallback (keep the offset) is never exercised by the generator.

There are two notes on the supplied rule text versus the constructor. Neither is a label defect:
- The rule text calls the design panel 'colour 1', but the generator picks the left-panel colour at random from {1,2,3,4,6,8}. The program therefore infers it from the panel corner instead of hard-coding 1.
- The text says the canvas is 'the most common colour in the grid'. The program identifies the canvas structurally instead, as the uniform panel.

I found no fixture contradiction of the uniform rule, and no hidden tie-break or indexing defect in the constructor.
